title: Parse host:port text
description: Implement parse_host_port(text). Parse a string of the form 'host:port' and return a tuple (host, port) where host is a str and port is an int. Raise TypeError if text is not a str. Strip surrounding whitespace from the whole string; raise ValueError on an empty string. The string must contain exactly one ':' (else ValueError); strip whitespace around both parts. Raise ValueError if the host is empty. The port part must be non-empty ASCII digits only (else ValueError): leading zeros are allowed, signs and decimal points are not. Convert to int and raise ValueError unless 1 <= port <= 65535. No further host validation is performed.
invariants: Exactly one ':' is required; zero or multiple colons are ValueError.
Port text like '00080' is valid and yields 80; '+80', '8.0', and '-1' are ValueError.
Boundary ports 1 and 65535 are valid; 0 and 65536 are ValueError.
Host is returned stripped; no further host validation is performed.
TypeError only for non-str input; every malformed string is ValueError.
